temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working extremely long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. Ethan invites Gary to a weekend retreat; Gary declines because there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dedicated but dangerously overworked, and that a short retreat could help him relax and gain perspective.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary refuses the retreat due to hospital workload, showing he is not ready or able to step away.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is deeply overloaded and resistant to taking a break; his health remains at risk.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, worried, and somewhat frustrated or helpless.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue supporting Gary and encouraging him to protect his health, and look for another way to help him address the overwork.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary behaving restlessly and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan confronts him; Gary says it is complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan with his problems.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is mainly overworked by hospital obligations and hoped the retreat would help him relax, though he does not yet know the deeper reasons.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's restlessness and avoidance, plus his comment that things are complicated, make Ethan suspect deeper personal or professional issues.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is carrying complicated burdens and is reluctant to share them, but needs nonjudgmental support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Encourage Gary to open up and offer help without judgment.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges. Gary agrees he could use help organizing his schedule and making time for himself.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has deeper, complicated struggles and is reluctant to burden others, but he does not yet know the specific causes.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Ethan learns the specific pressures of new departmental responsibilities plus personal challenges, and sees that Gary is willing to accept help.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary's overwork is understandable and improvable through prioritization, delegation, and better scheduling.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Help Gary prioritize tasks, delegate responsibilities, and organize his schedule to create better work-life balance.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan checks in with Gary and learns that Gary is making efforts to change. Gary reports feeling less overwhelmed and even had time for a movie last weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has started working toward better balance with his support, but still faces challenges and needs encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's reports and visible efforts show real improvement, less overwhelm, and reclaimed personal time.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is making meaningful progress and can continue improving with ongoing support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Continue regular check-ins, offer support and encouragement, and help with remaining challenges.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Ethan sees that Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and can manage on his own. Gary thanks Ethan and says he feels more in control.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has been making progress and still benefits from regular support and encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary has sustained a healthier balance for a year, manages independently, and feels in control.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary no longer needs intensive support and can maintain his balance on his own.
temporal_state_chain.intention: Step back from active support and let Gary manage independently, while remaining available if Gary needs him.
